purpose: Independent practice of E1.3 — matching halves and lines of symmetry.
student_learning_goal: I can make shapes with matching halves.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can make shapes with matching halves.
header.character_watermark: Compass Coco the Cat in the top-right corner with a folded shape. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Circle the shapes that have MATCHING HALVES.
parts.visual_layout: 8 shapes in a 2x4 grid. Some have matching halves (heart, square, circle, butterfly), some don't (letter F, apple bite, asymmetric blob, comma).

image_placeholders.description: A 2x4 grid of 8 shapes for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Top row: heart, square, letter F, asymmetric blob. Bottom row: butterfly, circle, comma, apple-with-bite. Each shape ~1.5in across, suitable for circling. Some have matching halves (heart, square, butterfly, circle), some don't (F, asymmetric blob, comma, apple with bite).
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P1_SHAPES at Part 1: instructions ask the child to circle shapes with matching halves. Keywords name the criteria.

parts.answer_key: CIRCLED (matching halves): heart, square, butterfly, circle. NOT CIRCLED: F, asymmetric blob, comma, apple-with-bite.

parts.student_instructions: Draw a line of symmetry on each shape.
parts.visual_layout: Four shapes stacked vertically: rectangle, equilateral triangle, maple leaf, star. Each has space for the child to draw a fold/symmetry line.

image_placeholders.description: Four shapes for symmetry lines for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Stacked vertically: rectangle, equilateral triangle, maple leaf (Canadian!), 5-point star. Each ~2in tall, generously spaced for the child to draw a vertical or other line of symmetry. No fill, just outlines.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P2_LINES at Part 2: instructions ask the child to draw symmetry lines. Keywords name the visual element.

parts.answer_key: Rectangle: vertical line through centre (or horizontal). Triangle: vertical line through apex. Maple leaf: vertical line through stem. Star: vertical line through one point.

parts.student_instructions: Draw a shape that has MATCHING HALVES. Show the line of symmetry.
parts.visual_layout: A blank drawing space (~5in × 3in) for the child's own design.

image_placeholders.description: A blank drawing rectangle for a Grade 1 worksheet, ~5in × 3in with thin solid border. Designed for the child to draw their own matching-halves shape and mark the line of symmetry.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P3_BLANK at Part 3: instructions ask the child to draw a matching-halves shape. Keywords name the criteria.

parts.answer_key: Any symmetric shape with the line clearly drawn (heart, butterfly, leaf, oval, etc.).

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw a shape with TWO lines of symmetry.
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation artifact. Use Part 1 as the formative signal — children who correctly identify all 4 symmetric shapes have grasped the concept.
